official_measurement_examples.name: Three consent routes
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance distinguishes advertisements needing neither deemed nor express consent, advertisements with deemed consent, and advertisements requiring express consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Express-consent determination period
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance states an LPA decision on express advertisement consent must be given within 8 weeks unless the applicant agrees in writing to a longer period.

official_measurement_examples.name: Amenity and public safety
official_measurement_examples.fact: Advertisement-control decisions are exercised principally in the interests of amenity and public safety under the statutory regime.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal deadline
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK appeal guidance says an advertisement-consent appeal against a decision generally must be made within 8 weeks of the decision notice.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal fee
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance states there is no fee for appealing an advertisement-consent decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: Deemed-consent restriction
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance explains that deemed consent can be restricted in defined areas through the statutory direction process.

official_measurement_examples.name: Separate listed-building regime
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance notes that other statutory permissions such as listed building consent can still be required even where advertisement consent rules are satisfied.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 appeal template currency
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Planning Inspectorate model notification letter for advertisement appeals was updated on 29 April 2026.
